tools.why: Enables the pdftotext extraction backend — the fastest path for text-layer PDFs, and the only one needing no Python environment or network access.

Rasterises PDF pages to images. Required by the tesseract OCR backend, the ollama vision backend, and the terminal page-preview renderer — without it those three are unavailable regardless of their own tools.
Enables OCR extraction for scanned or image-only PDFs, which have no text layer for pdftotext to read. Needs pdftoppm as well.
Carries the HTTP requests for the claude backend (Anthropic API) and the ollama backend's daemon check. Usually already present.
Enables the ollama backend: a local vision model reads rasterised pages, so scanned PDFs can be extracted without sending anything to a cloud API. Needs pdftoppm and a running daemon.
Renders PDF pages as images inside the terminal for :PdfPort preview, on terminals without their own image protocol.

An alternative terminal image renderer for the page preview, drawing real pixels over the terminal on X11/Wayland where chafa can only approximate them in cells. Optional: chafa is the default and needs nothing extra.
Enables the img2pdf creation producer — the lossless first choice for image -> PDF (embeds JPEG/PNG data unchanged instead of recompressing).
Enables the magick creation producer — pragmatic default for image -> PDF, handles multi-image -> multi-page natively.
Enables the pandoc creation producer for markdown/text -> PDF. Needs one PDF engine as well (tectonic/typst/xelatex/lualatex/pdflatex).
Enables the weasyprint creation producer — first choice for html -> PDF (clean CSS Paged Media support).
Enables the soffice creation producer for office (docx/odt/xlsx/pptx) -> PDF, one call covers all four formats.
Enables the qpdf producer — first choice for pdfport.merge() (small, exact, no page-content re-encoding).
Enables the pdftk producer — pdfport.merge() fallback #2, behind qpdf.
Enables the ghostscript producer — pdfport.merge() fallback #3 (last resort: recompresses page content).
